summary: Metal Forest Service cab built 1965 to replace an L-4 ground house; a 1946 newspaper describes an earlier wood-and-glass tower; reported lightning fires for the Forest Service in August 2026.

facts.design: CL-100 to CL-106 series 14x14-foot metal flat-top cab with metal catwalk on a 10-foot cinder block base with storage room (register)

access.note: No visitor rules appear in the sources read. The register does not address access, and the lookout reported lightning fires for the Forest Service on August 3, 2026, so it is an active working post.

events.note: Rangers at the site had a telephone link into the Forest Service system and tested heliograph signals with Rabbit Mountain
Earlier L-4 ground house, dated 1932 by the register; replaced in 1965
Santa Fe New Mexican item describes a lookout working a small wood-and-glass tower anchored with wire cables; gives the peak as 11,000 feet
Standard Plan metal cab with metal catwalk on a 10-foot cinder block base with storage room
The 1965 cab replaced the L-4 ground house
Evaluated for the thematic National Register nomination and found not eligible due to age
Forest Fire Lookout Association report recommends re-evaluation for the National Register now that the cab is 55 years old
Cerro Pelado Fire on the Jemez Ranger District in spring 2022, caused by a holdover from the Pino West Piles prescribed fire; the release does not say the fire reached the lookout
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on May 22, 2022
Forest Service updates credit two lightning fires reported on August 3, 2026 to the Cerro Pelado Lookout

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the 1965 cab replaced a 1932 L-4 ground house. A 1946 newspaper item quoted by West Lookouts describes a small wood-and-glass tower. The two do not match and this is not resolved; the story says so.
The 1946 item gives the peak as 11,000 feet; the register gives 10,012 ft (3,052 m). The register figure is used.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m of 11.0 does not appear in any source read (the register gives no height), so it is omitted. The brief's 'steel-cab' wording is 'metal' in the register. Staffing 'staffed' as of 2026-08-03 is inferred from Forest Service updates that credit two lightning-fire reports to the Cerro Pelado Lookout; no source gives staffing hours or season. The 2022 Cerro Pelado Fire is a separate event on the Jemez district; no source says it reached the lookout. Visitor access was not found in any source, so 'restricted' is an editorial judgement. The register PDF photo (2010, courtesy Janie O'Rourke) has no licence, so it is not listed under photos. The 1946 'wood-and-glass tower' conflicts with the register's ground house; unresolved.
